title: Jewellery Wholesale in Pakistan: Prices, Quality & Where to Buy
summary: Jewellery wholesale in Pakistan: what drives the price, how to spot bad plating, minimum orders, and how to buy jewellery wholesale with COD.
body_markdown:
Wholesale jewellery in Pakistan usually means one of three things: buying by the dozen from Karachi's Saddar or Lahore's Anarkali, ordering a bulk lot from a local supplier, or importing directly from China. Which one makes sense depends less on the price per piece than on how much stock you are willing to hold. This guide covers what jewellery actually costs at wholesale, what drives that price, how to judge quality before you commit, and how to buy without a minimum order at all.


## What "wholesale" actually means for jewellery here


In most Pakistani jewellery supply, "wholesale" is a quantity threshold rather than a separate catalogue. A supplier quotes one rate for a single piece and a lower one per piece once you take a dozen, a gross, or a full carton. The jump between those tiers is where your margin lives.


Two distinctions matter before you shop:


- **Artificial vs imitation vs semi-precious.** Artificial (costume) jewellery is base metal with plating and acrylic or glass stones. Imitation aims to copy a gold or silver look closely. Semi-precious brings real stones. They sit at different price points and attract different buyers — decide which you are selling before you compare rates.
- **Sets vs singles.** Bridal and party sets carry a much higher ticket than everyday earrings or rings, but they move slower and tie up more cash per unit.


## Where Pakistani jewellery wholesale actually comes from


Follow the supply chain back and most costume jewellery sold here arrives from the same place.


**Local wholesale markets.** Saddar in Karachi, Anarkali and Shah Alam in Lahore, and Raja Bazaar in Rawalpindi are the traditional hubs. You can see and handle stock before buying, which is a genuine advantage with jewellery, and you can restock quickly. The trade-off is that most of what you are looking at was imported by someone else, so you are paying their margin on top.


**Local online suppliers.** Marketplaces and supplier lists let you order without travelling. Delivery is quick, and you can start small.


**Direct from China.** This is where the bulk of costume jewellery originates. Buying direct removes the importer's margin, which is the single biggest saving available — but the usual import friction applies unless someone handles it for you. ## What actually drives the price


Jewellery pricing is unusually opaque because two pieces that look identical can differ sharply in cost. The drivers, roughly in order of impact:


- **Plating thickness and type.** Gold-tone plating varies enormously. Thin plating is cheaper and tarnishes faster — this is the number one source of customer complaints and returns.
- **Base metal.** Brass and copper alloys behave differently against skin than cheaper zinc alloys. Anything that discolours skin or triggers reactions will cost you repeat business.
- **Stone type and setting.** Glued stones are cheaper than prong-set. Glue fails; prongs mostly do not.
- **Finish and clasp quality.** Clasps are the first thing to break, and a broken clasp turns a sale into a return.
- **Order quantity.** The per-piece rate drops at each tier, which is why suppliers push you upward.


A practical point that catches new resellers: the cheapest quote in a market is usually cheap because of the first two items on that list, not because the seller is generous.


## How to judge quality before you commit


Jewellery is one of the easiest categories to sample and one of the most expensive to get wrong at volume. Before a bulk order:


- **Buy one piece first.** Wear it, wash your hands with it on, leave it out for a couple of weeks. Plating problems show up fast.
- **Check the clasp and the joints.** Open and close it twenty times.
- **Look at the back, not the front.** Finishing quality on the reverse tells you how the piece was actually made.
- **Photograph it yourself in daylight.** Supplier photos are heavily edited across this whole category, and the gap between the listing photo and the item is the most common reason a jewellery order disappoints.


## Minimum orders and how much stock to start with


Traditional wholesale wants you to commit. A market supplier may not quote you a real rate below a dozen; an importer may want a carton. That is fine when you know what sells and painful when you do not.


The honest advice for a first run is to spread a small budget across several designs rather than going deep on one. Jewellery taste is specific, and the design you personally like is often not the one that moves. Testing ten designs at one or two pieces each teaches you more than fifty pieces of a single style — and leaves you far less dead stock if you guess wrong.


That is exactly the approach minimums are designed to prevent, which is why no-minimum sourcing matters more in this category than in most.

## Frequently asked questions


**What is the minimum order for jewellery wholesale in Pakistan?** Market suppliers typically quote real wholesale rates from a dozen pieces upward, and importers often want more.[Markaz China](https://www.markaz.app/china) has no minimum order.


**Where is the cheapest place to buy wholesale jewellery in Pakistan?** On sticker price, buying direct from China is usually cheapest because it removes the local importer's margin. Local markets win on speed and on being able to inspect stock before paying.


**How do I stop plated jewellery from tarnishing?** Mostly you buy better plating in the first place — thin plating tarnishes whatever the customer does. Sample a piece and wear-test it for a fortnight before ordering at volume.


**Is artificial jewellery profitable to resell in Pakistan?** It can be, because the ticket is low and buyers repeat. The margin depends on sourcing close to the factory and on not holding dead stock in designs that did not move.


**Can I buy wholesale jewellery with cash on delivery?** Local suppliers sometimes offer it. Cross-border platforms generally do not. Markaz China offers cash on delivery in rupees in major Pakistani cities.
